@aio:claude-modules: ## Redis cache
`cacheService` (`src/services/cache.service.ts`) is a thin, fail-open wrapper around
Redis: every method checks `redis.isReady` first and never throws — if Redis is down, reads
miss and writes are skipped, so the app keeps serving from Postgres instead of failing the
request. Invalidation is by **version counter**, not key deletion: `bumpVersion(resource)`
does an `INCR` on a small `meta:version:<resource>` key, and every previously-built
versioned key for that resource simply stops being asked for again — no `SCAN`/`DEL` on the
hot path (`deleteByPattern` exists as an emergency-only escape hatch).
**Reading:** mount `readCache({ ttlSeconds, buildKey })` in front of a `GET` route.
`buildKey` returns `null` to bypass caching for a given request (e.g. an uncacheable query
combination) or a key built with `cacheService.buildVersionedKey(resource, ...)`. On a hit
it responds immediately, skipping the controller; on a miss it stashes
`{ key, ttlSeconds }` on `res.locals.cache` and calls `next()`.
**Writing:** call `sendCached(res, payload)` instead of `res.json(payload)` in the
controller behind it — it writes `payload` to the cached key (if `readCache` set one) and
sends the response in the same call, so caching what you actually send can't drift into
caching something else.
**Invalidating:** in the write controller for that resource, call
`cacheService.bumpVersion(resource, { segments: [...] })` with the same `segments` used to
build the read key's *version* scope (not the full key — params like `skip`/`take` stay out
of the version scope so one bump invalidates every paginated/filtered variant at once).
